description: Tick trades by UTC date. Retrieve available trades for a stock, fund, currency, or futures symbol; other symbol types return 400 `unsupported_symbol_type`. Today's and tomorrow's UTC dates return a rolling snapshot, with 24 hours by default; the previous six dates return their UTC calendar days. U.S.-listed stocks and funds use New York dates instead: today's or tomorrow's date returns the New York day so far unless `window` is set. For continuous futures, 1! uses today's front contract and 2! uses today's next contract for every requested date. The response code identifies the selected dated contract. → Returns {code, bar_type: '1T', last_update?, as_of?, window_start?, series: [{time, close, type?, volume?}], error?, message?}. Point time is Unix seconds; last_update, as_of, and window_start are Unix milliseconds. For today or tomorrow's date, window selects 3h/6h/9h/12h/15h/18h/21h/24h (default 24h; without it, U.S.-listed stocks and funds return the New York day so far); historical dates ignore window. Rolling snapshots include inclusive window_start and exclusive as_of. Empty results return series: [] with an error and message. Use filter to summarize trades or store=json with output_file to save the response.

date.description: UTC date in YYYY-MM-DD format; U.S.-listed stocks and funds use New York dates. Today and the previous six dates are supported; until midnight, tomorrow's date returns the same data as today's.

filter.description: (Optional) JSONata expression to return only the fields or rows you need. See https://jsonata.org for syntax.

output_dir.description: Directory for stored response when output_file is not set.

store.description: Store the response locally instead of returning it. Default is none. csv is only supported for get_symbol_series.

symbol.description: Symbol in Exchange:Symbol format (e.g., NASDAQ:AAPL, NYSE:TSLA). You can search for this symbol code using the /v3/symbols/search endpoint.

window.description: Rolling duration for today's or tomorrow's date. Without it, U.S.-listed stocks and funds return the New York day so far; other symbols use 24 hours. Ignored for historical dates.

name: get_symbol_trades
